links.reason: Righteousness brings wealth in one; in the other, riches and saintliness are two things with nothing in common.
links.quoteA: it bringeth wealth also
links.quoteB: Riches is one thing and Saintliness is quite another

links.reason: The one who lives home life well is first among all who strive, yet those who renounce completely have arrived and all others are caught in a net.
links.quoteA: The one who lives home life as it should be lived is first among all who strive
links.quoteB: All others are deluded, and caught in a net

links.reason: Nothing is grander than a woman firm in chastity, yet a woman’s heart serves elsewhere as the very measure of how friendship shifts.
links.quoteA: strong in the strength of her chastity
links.quoteB: alter even as the heart of a woman

links.reason: The soul returns to a body for the sake of love in one; the other asks why a soul should shelter in so worthless a body at all.
links.quoteA: to taste again of love that the soul hath consented
links.quoteB: taketh shelter in this worthless body

links.reason: Loss will always come, whatever your heart does, yet ruin is said to be rare for anyone who doesn’t stray aside to do evil.
links.quoteA: Loss and gain will always come
links.quoteB: ruin is rare for anyone who doesn’t stray aside to do evil

links.reason: A single evil word turns all your good bad, yet the noble may say things without goodness, so long as they say nothing useless.
links.quoteA: If a single evil word does its harm, the good you have done turns bad
links.quoteB: Let the noble say things without goodness if they will

links.reason: Those who punish a wrong count for nothing and those who bear it are kept like gold, yet those who don’t crush their foes’ pride won’t live to draw breath.
links.quoteA: Those who bear it are wrapped up and kept like gold
links.quoteB: Those who fail to crush the pride of their foes surely won’t live

links.reason: Smiling falsely to a face while ruining behind the back is worse than doing wrong, yet it is the advice for those who make much of you and despise you.
links.quoteA: to ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely to their face
links.quoteB: make them laugh, and within that friendship hold them so that it dies

links.reason: Taking is bad even if it were a good road, yet to beg from those who hide nothing is called like giving.
links.quoteA: Even if it were a good road, taking is bad
links.quoteB: Begging is like giving

links.reason: Never judge by appearance, warns one; the other holds that the face shows what fills the heart as surely as crystal shows a colour.
links.quoteA: by their acts and not by their appearance
links.quoteB: doth the face alter and show that which overfloweth the heart

links.reason: A lie counts as truthfulness if it brings good, yet what the worthy condemn stays forbidden even when the mother who bore you goes hungry.
links.quoteA: Even a lie counts as truthfulness, if it brings good with no fault in it
links.quoteB: Even if you see the mother who bore you go hungry, don’t do what the worthy condemn

links.reason: Nothing at all is better than truthfulness, says one, yet the other ranks not killing first and puts not lying second.
links.quoteA: nothing at all is better than truthfulness
links.quoteB: Not killing stands alone as good. Next after it, not lying is good

links.reason: Someone who prizes anger will surely be ruined, yet the wise are shown burning within and watching for their time.
links.quoteA: Someone who prizes anger will be ruined
links.quoteB: They watch for the time and burn within

links.reason: Killing brings every wrong with it, says one; in the other, the many his lord has killed, now standing in stone, are a warrior’s boast.
links.quoteA: Killing brings with it every action of the other kind
links.quoteB: Many have stood before him, and now they stand in stone

links.reason: Don’t take another life even to save your own, yet a ruler who punishes the wicked with death is likened to someone pulling weeds from a green crop.
links.quoteA: don’t do what takes another sweet life
links.quoteB: A ruler who punishes the wicked with death is like someone pulling weeds from a green crop

links.reason: Two roads to a full life: renounce early and delights follow, or amass great wealth and the other aims of life come within reach.
links.quoteA: If thou want joy, renounce early
links.quoteB: both the other objects of life are within his reach

links.reason: Refusing to let go of attachments brings grief that will not let go of you, yet the whole world loves the man whose affection never lets go.
links.quoteA: holdeth on to attachments and giveth not them up
links.quoteB: loveth another with a deathless affection

links.reason: Wisdom means aiming to escape birth into this world in one, and going along with the ways of this world in the other.
links.quoteA: the part of Wisdom to desire to escape the folly called birth
links.quoteB: a part of wisdom to conform to the ways of the world

links.reason: Drive comes because fate is bringing wealth, or prosperity comes because someone’s drive never wavers: each makes the other’s effect its cause.
links.quoteA: The fate that brings you wealth also brings the drive to work
links.quoteB: Prosperity asks the way and goes by itself to someone whose drive never wavers

links.reason: However much you study, the understanding you were born with wins out, yet understanding is also said to flow as far as you learn.
links.quoteA: the understanding you were born with still wins out
links.quoteB: People’s understanding flows as far as they learn

links.reason: The understanding you were born with wins out over all your study, yet people’s understanding is also said to take on the nature of their company.
links.quoteA: the understanding you were born with still wins out
links.quoteB: People’s understanding takes on the nature of their company

links.reason: What fate denies won’t stay however you guard it, yet acting in step with the season is a rope that ties good fortune down.
links.quoteA: What isn’t yours by fate won’t stay, however hard you guard it
links.quoteB: a rope that ties good fortune down so that it can’t leave

links.reason: Fate gets there first even as you plan around it, yet those who plan are said to get just what they planned, if they are firm.
links.quoteA: Even as you plan a way around it, it gets there first
links.quoteB: Those who plan will get what they planned, just as they planned it, if they are firm

links.reason: The wise won’t accept an unlearned man’s cleverness even when it is very good, yet understanding is seeing the reality in what you hear, from anyone.
links.quoteA: Even when an unlearned man’s cleverness is very good, the wise don’t accept it
links.quoteB: Whatever you hear, from whoever’s mouth, understanding is seeing the reality in it

links.reason: The wise man is at home with all the world in one; in the other, men of worth are afraid of low company.
links.quoteA: The wise man is sociable with all the world
links.quoteB: Men of worth fear vulgar company

links.reason: Saying you will think after you commit is a mistake, yet those who strive without delay for their family are promised success without planning.
links.quoteA: To say you will think after you have committed is a mistake
links.quoteB: success comes of itself, without planning

links.reason: Many who didn’t know their strength broke halfway, yet you are told never to call a task too hard, because effort will give you greatness.
links.quoteA: set out on a surge of zeal and broke halfway
links.quoteB: Don’t lose heart and say “This is too hard.”

links.reason: Climbing past the tip of a branch costs your life, yet all your thoughts are to be of rising higher, since even failing has the nature of not failing.
links.quoteA: Those who have climbed to the tip of a branch and try to go further will lose their life
links.quoteB: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

links.reason: The one at a ruler’s side must tell him what is good for him, however he takes it, yet those around him are told to say what isn’t disliked, and to please.
links.quoteA: it is the duty of the one at his side to tell him what is good for him
links.quoteB: say what is needed and not disliked, in a way that pleases

links.reason: Everyone scorns those who have nothing, yet the world is also said to count no lack as poverty except a lack of understanding.
links.quoteA: Everyone scorns those who have nothing
links.quoteB: The world does not count any other lack as poverty

links.reason: A spear that missed an elephant beats an arrow that hit a hare, yet whoever won’t take the small prize of an easy fight will never win glory.
links.quoteA: Better to hold a spear that missed an elephant than an arrow that hit a hare
links.quoteB: If you won’t take the small prize of fighting an unlearned man, glory will never come to you

links.reason: An enemy can never rid his heart of hate, yet the tactful prince is praised for turning enemies into allies.
links.quoteA: it is impossible for an enemy to cast off the hate in his heart
links.quoteB: convert enemies into allies

links.reason: The enmity of a man who does a task all wrong is worth paying for, yet the very next chapter says no one should want enmity, even in jest.
links.quoteA: Even if you must pay for it, be sure to get the enmity
links.quoteB: No one should want it, even in jest

links.reason: Uprightness and shame come by nature only to those of good family, yet birth is the same for all and only what they do sets them apart.
links.quoteA: Only in those born of a good family do uprightness and shame come together by nature
links.quoteB: Birth is the same for every living being

links.reason: When your means shrink you must stand tall, yet those raising a family are warned that thinking of their pride will ruin it.
links.quoteA: When your means shrink, stand tall
links.quoteB: Be idle and think of your pride, and it is ruined

links.reason: Trailing after those who scorn you is pointless in one; in the other the lovesick cannot even conceive of the pride that would refuse to follow.
links.quoteA: fawning on men that despise him
links.quoteB: a thing unknown to the lovesick fair

links.reason: Character keeps poverty from being any disgrace in one; in the other want forces even the well-born into abject speech.
links.quoteA: Poverty is no disgrace to a man
links.quoteB: Want will drive even men of high family to forget their dignity

links.reason: Begging from those who hide nothing is like giving, says one chapter; the next says not begging is worth ten million times more, even there.
links.quoteA: Begging is like giving
links.quoteB: not begging is worth ten million times more

links.reason: Without people who beg the world would be a wooden puppet; the next chapter curses its maker if anyone must live by begging.
links.quoteA: Without people who beg, this great cool world would be a wooden puppet
links.quoteB: wanted people to live even by begging, let him wander far and perish

links.reason: Remembering their days together is how she stays alive, yet keeping him in her heart, she says later, will only cost her more of her beauty.
links.quoteA: I live by remembering the days I was with him
links.quoteB: If we keep in our heart the one who left us and won’t come near, we will lose still more of our beauty

links.reason: Full desire leaves no room for a millet seed of sulking, yet sulking is called the joy of desire.
links.quoteA: you must not sulk even by a millet seed
links.quoteB: Sulking is the joy of desire

links.reason: Softens the flat denial that the envious gain: a crooked heart does sometimes prosper, and that gives you something to think about.
links.quoteA: When a crooked heart prospers
links.quoteB: the envious have no gain

links.reason: Patience may keep your integrity with you, but holding back anger only counts where the anger could take effect.
links.quoteA: Whoever holds back anger where it can take effect truly holds it back
links.quoteB: guard your patience and live by it

links.reason: Striving may see the back of fate, but only if it is made the right way: effort that isn’t will crack, however many stand guard.
links.quoteA: Effort not made the right way will crack
links.quoteB: Those who strive without faltering and without delay will see the back of fate itself

links.reason: Doing good however you can isn’t enough: even good can go wrong if it isn’t done knowing each person’s nature.
links.quoteA: Even doing good can go wrong, if you don’t do it knowing each person’s nature
links.quoteB: do righteous deeds everywhere they can be done

links.reason: A fortress serves those who fear and look after themselves, but for those who are only afraid there is no fort at all.
links.quoteA: There is no fort for those who are afraid
links.quoteB: of value to those who fear and look after themselves

links.reason: Punishing wrongdoing is no stain on a ruler and is his work, but he must look into the wrong fairly and punish to fit it.
links.quoteA: looks into a wrong fairly and punishes to fit it
links.quoteB: punish wrongdoing is no stain on a ruler

links.reason: Living up to what you have learned isn’t the end of it: even when you know the methods, you must know the nature of the world before you act.
links.quoteA: Even when you know the methods, know the nature of the world and then act
links.quoteB: Once you have learned it, live up to it

links.reason: Thinking before acting is required, but thinking must end: once a decision is reached, further delay is itself the fault.
links.quoteA: it is wrong to delay the execution thereof
links.quoteB: Decide not upon any action except after careful deliberation

links.reason: Only kin are said to cherish old ties when you have lost everything, but an enemy within who is close by kinship brings harms that lead towards death.
links.quoteA: When an enemy within appears who is close by kinship, it brings many harms
links.quoteB: Only kin go on cherishing old ties even when you have lost everything

links.reason: Gaining renown is a duty, but not at any price: those who want glory with strength of character won’t do anything unworthy even for it.
links.quoteA: won’t do anything unworthy, even for glory
links.quoteB: it is a disgrace for everyone on earth not to gain the legacy called renown

links.reason: Having no craving is no guarantee against suffering: if those who plough fold their hands, even those who have given up all desire can’t stand firm.
links.quoteA: If those who plough fold their hands, even those who say they have given up all desire can’t stand firm
links.quoteB: Those without craving have no suffering

links.reason: A quarrel may be sweeter than making love, but only in the right amount: drawn out, a sulk is like a little too much salt.
links.quoteA: A sulk is like the right amount of salt. Drawing it out is like a little too much
links.quoteB: a quarrel is sweeter than making love

links.reason: Greatness is defined the same way in both: the great are those who do what is hard to do.
links.quoteA: Those who do what is hard to do are great
links.quoteB: The great will carry out hard deeds

links.reason: Do good now, because death will not wait: the day of death in one, the hiccup in the throat in the other.
links.quoteA: Don’t say “I’ll see to it some other day.”
links.quoteB: Before your tongue is stilled and the hiccup rises, rush to do good deeds

links.reason: Outward beauty counts for nothing beside an inner grace, which is love in one and character in the other.
links.quoteA: Of what avail is a lovely outside
links.quoteB: the comeliness of the body addeth nothing

links.reason: What a service is worth lies not in the act but in the person it reaches: the worth of the guest in one, of those who received it in the other.
links.quoteA: It is measured by the worth of the guest
links.quoteB: It is the worth of those who received it

links.reason: Wealth guarded and never used comes to nothing: the hoarder ends with nothing to hold on to, or as a dead man beside it.
links.quoteA: After anxious guarding they will say “We have nothing to hold on to”
links.quoteB: He stores up great heaps of wealth and doesn’t eat from it. He is a dead man

links.reason: Forgetting a wrong goes further than forgiving it: nobility forgets at once, and if you can forget, that is better than pardon.
links.quoteA: It is good to forget what is not good, that very day
links.quoteB: Forgetting it is better still

links.reason: Turn down wealth that costs you your integrity, whatever profit it offers: honest poverty is far better.
links.quoteA: let go at once of gain that comes from leaving the middle
links.quoteB: Better the deep poverty of the worthy than prosperity gained by wearing disgrace

links.reason: Both single out speech as the thing above all to guard, because suffering, and even ruin, ride on its slips.
links.quoteA: Whatever else you fail to guard, guard your tongue
links.quoteB: guard carefully against any slip in your speech

links.reason: Envy and prosperity never meet, stated once as a rule and once as what has never yet happened.
links.quoteA: the envious have no gain
links.quoteB: No one has grown great through envy

links.reason: Learning doesn’t cure folly: much learning can leave you without understanding, and the greatest fool of all is a teacher with no self-control.
links.quoteA: may learn much, but they are still without understanding
links.quoteB: No one is a greater fool than someone who studies, understands, teaches others, and still has no self-control

links.reason: Worth is the way to beat an enemy: defeat those who wrong you by your own worth, and bowing is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around.
links.quoteA: Defeat by your own worth those who wrong you
links.quoteB: That is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around

links.reason: Turn on your own faults the eye you keep for others’ and no harm can reach you, said first to everyone and later to the ruler.
links.quoteA: If you could see your own faults as you see strangers’ faults
links.quoteB: If a ruler removes his own faults first, and then looks at those of others

links.reason: Injuring others is what brings ills upon you, so whoever wants to be free of ills should injure no one.
links.quoteA: If you don’t want painful things to strike you down, don’t do evil things to others
links.quoteB: Those who want to be free of pain cause none

links.reason: Goodness outlasts the means for it: those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping, and old families keep their good nature as their giving shrinks.
links.quoteA: Even when they have little room to give, those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping others
links.quoteB: Even when what they have to give has shrunk, those of an old family don’t part from their good nature

links.reason: Your own experience of fear and pain is the brake on hurting others: imagine trembling before a stronger, or recall what you have felt.
links.quoteA: think of yourself before those stronger
links.quoteB: What you know to be painful, you must not do to anyone else

links.reason: Looks are no measure of a person, shown by the cruel arrow and the bent harp in one and by the axle pin of a great chariot in the other.
links.quoteA: Judge people the same way, by what they do
links.quoteB: Don’t scorn people for how they look

links.reason: Wealth won by stealing or deceit can’t hold, however it seems to grow: it perishes in one, and it is water in a pot of raw clay in the other.
links.quoteA: seems to grow, then perishes beyond all measure
links.quoteB: like pouring water into a pot of raw clay

links.reason: The worthy repay injury with good: it is the only punishment worth the name, and the very proof of their superiority.
links.quoteA: do them such good that they are ashamed
links.quoteB: What use is worth, if you don’t do kindness even to those who have done you harm?

links.reason: Almost word for word: understanding is seeing the reality, in every thing and from every mouth.
links.quoteA: understanding is seeing the reality in it
links.quoteB: understanding is seeing the reality in it

links.reason: Coming fortune or ruin shows first in the mind: luck widens a man’s wits and his patience, doom dulls him and sets him quarrelling.
links.quoteA: when Fortune is about to smile she first expandeth the intelligence
links.quoteB: When fortune is about to smile on a man he will ignore all provocation

links.reason: Being easy to reach decides how a ruler stands: with it his land is praised above all others, without it he falls by himself.
links.quoteA: If a ruler is easy to see and not harsh in speech, his land will be praised above all others
links.quoteB: A ruler who isn’t easy to reach, and doesn’t look into things and give justice, will sink low and fall by himself

links.reason: A ruler lasts by bearing what stings: the world rests under one who bears bitter words, and one with no one to rebuke him falls.
links.quoteA: a ruler with the character to bear words bitter to his ears
links.quoteB: A ruler with no one to rebuke him has no protection

links.reason: One rule of action stated twice: weigh the cost, the obstacles and the gain to come, and only then act.
links.quoteA: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained, and the profit it will bring later, then act
links.quoteB: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach when it is done, and then act

links.reason: No war should begin before it is prepared for: think through every side of it first, and find the ground for a siege first.
links.quoteA: To march out without thinking through every side of it
links.quoteB: Start nothing and scorn no one until you have found the ground for a siege

links.reason: Rule stays sound only if the ruler looks into it daily: do so every day, or watch the land go to ruin day by day.
links.quoteA: Let the ruler look into it every day
links.quoteB: When a ruler doesn’t look into things daily and do justice, his land goes to ruin day by day

links.reason: A fort is only as good as those in it: there is no fort for those who are afraid, and none for those with no excellence in action.
links.quoteA: There is no fort for those who are afraid
links.quoteB: with those who have no excellence in action it is no fortress

links.reason: What is gained through others’ tears is lost to tears: the tears of those who suffer wear away wealth, and what was taken with tears leaves with tears.
links.quoteA: are they not the weapon that wears away wealth?
links.quoteB: All that was taken with tears leaves with tears

links.reason: The world keeps going only because of gentle ways, called kindly regard in one and courtesy in the other.
links.quoteA: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty called kindly regard
links.quoteB: The world goes on because of the courteous

links.reason: A high aim that fails beats a low one that succeeds: rising thoughts don’t truly fail, and a spear that missed an elephant outdoes an arrow in a hare.
links.quoteA: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing
links.quoteB: Better to hold a spear that missed an elephant than an arrow that hit a hare

links.reason: Learning that cannot be put across is wasted: it is a flower without scent in one, and good for nothing in the other.
links.quoteA: like flowers that bloom in clusters but have no scent
links.quoteB: of no use, however much they have learned

links.reason: What lies within shows through: the heart in the face, as crystal shows what is beside it, and something in her adornment, like a thread through a bead.
links.quoteA: the face shows what is strongest in the heart
links.quoteB: Like the thread that shows through a bead, something shows through this young woman’s adornment

links.reason: Good speech is wasted on the petty: don’t speak there even by forgetting, since trying to show a man who can’t see leaves you seeing nothing.
links.quoteA: don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting
links.quoteB: Whoever tries to show a man who can’t see ends up seeing nothing himself

links.reason: No prize justifies a stain on your name: not piled-up millions for those of good family, not the wide world for the best of people.
links.quoteA: Even for piled-up millions, those of good family won’t do anything that lowers them
links.quoteB: won’t want the wide world unless they have shame as their fence

links.reason: Life is not worth buying with disgrace: what would lower you stays forbidden even when your survival depends on it.
links.quoteA: Even things you can’t do without, give them up if they would lower you
links.quoteB: They won’t give up shame for life

links.reason: Goodness decides what poverty does: with worth there is no disgrace, without righteousness a man is a stranger even to the mother who bore him.
links.quoteA: Having nothing is no disgrace, if you have the strength called worth
links.quoteB: looked at as a stranger, even by the mother who bore him

links.reason: Desire outdoes liquor in the same way, heard first from him and then from her: liquor must be drunk, but desire delights at a glance.
links.quoteA: It can’t delight those who merely see, as desire does
links.quoteB: toddy can’t do this, but desire can

links.reason: Answering the village’s talk that he has left her, she says he has not: he lives in her heart, and she sees him in her dreams.
links.quoteA: This town says he lives apart from me
links.quoteB: They say he left me in waking life

links.reason: Tenderness itself has become a warning: she cannot enjoy his embrace or his kindness for fear that he means to leave.
links.quoteA: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave
links.quoteB: He comforts me so fully and joins me so gladly, but in it I see myself bearing pain again

links.reason: Having him brings no relief: the fear of losing him spoils the very moment of having him.
links.quoteA: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave
links.quoteB: when it has him it fears parting

links.reason: Her slipped bangles do the telling: what her arms have lost tells everyone that he has gone, and how cruel he is.
links.quoteA: Won’t these bangles slipping from my forearm spread the word
links.quoteB: Your arms, their bangles gone and their old beauty withered, tell of the cruelty of a cruel man
